"""
Performance drift detection for ML models.

Detects degradation in classification and regression metrics by comparing
reference (baseline) values against current (production) values.
"""

import logging
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import ClassVar

import numpy as np

logger = logging.getLogger("dlh_ai")

DriftResult = dict[str, float | bool | str | dict[str, float]]


@dataclass
class PerformanceDrift:
    """
    Performance drift detector for ML model metrics.

    All detection logic lives inside this class. Instantiate once with a
    threshold and call metric methods directly on the instance.

    Parameters
    ----------
    threshold : float, optional
        Default minimum absolute change required to flag drift. Must be a
        positive finite number. Default is ``0.05``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``threshold`` is not a positive finite number.
    """

    _EPSILON: ClassVar[float] = 1e-10

    threshold: float = field(default=0.05)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not np.isfinite(self.threshold) or self.threshold <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"threshold must be a positive finite number, got {self.threshold}."
            )

    @staticmethod
    def _validate_metric_value(value: float, name: str) -> None:
        if not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
            raise TypeError(
                f"'{name}' must be a numeric value, got {type(value).__name__}."
            )
        if not np.isfinite(value):
            raise ValueError(f"'{name}' must be a finite number, got {value}.")

    @staticmethod
    def _severity(abs_change: float) -> str:
        if abs_change < 0.02:
            return "low"
        if abs_change < 0.05:
            return "medium"
        if abs_change < 0.10:
            return "high"
        return "critical"

    def _scalar_drift(
        self,
        metric_name: str,
        result_key: str,
        reference: float,
        current: float,
        threshold: float,
    ) -> DriftResult:
        change = current - reference
        abs_change = abs(change)
        drift_detected = bool(abs_change > threshold)
        return {
            "metric_name": metric_name,
            "reference_value": float(reference),
            "current_value": float(current),
            result_key: float(change),
            "threshold": float(threshold),
            "drift_detected": drift_detected,
            "drift_severity": self._severity(abs_change) if drift_detected else "none",
        }

    def accuracy_drift(
        self,
        reference_accuracy: float,
        current_accuracy: float,
        threshold: float | None = None,
    ) -> DriftResult:
        """
        Detect drift in model accuracy.

        Parameters
        ----------
        reference_accuracy : float
            Baseline accuracy value in [0, 1].
        current_accuracy : float
            Current accuracy value in [0, 1].
        threshold : float or None, optional
            Minimum absolute change to flag drift. Falls back to
            ``self.threshold`` when ``None``.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            ``metric_name`` : str
                Always ``"Accuracy Drift"``.
            ``reference_value`` : float
                Baseline accuracy.
            ``current_value`` : float
                Current accuracy.
            ``accuracy_change`` : float
                Signed change (current − reference).
            ``threshold`` : float
                Threshold used.
            ``drift_detected`` : bool
                ``True`` when ``|accuracy_change| > threshold``.
            ``drift_severity`` : str
                ``"none"`` | ``"low"`` | ``"medium"`` | ``"high"`` | ``"critical"``.
        """
        t = threshold if threshold is not None else self.threshold
        self._validate_metric_value(reference_accuracy, "reference_accuracy")
        self._validate_metric_value(current_accuracy, "current_accuracy")
        logger.debug(
            "Checking accuracy drift: %.4f -> %.4f",
            reference_accuracy,
            current_accuracy,
        )
        return self._scalar_drift(
            "Accuracy Drift", "accuracy_change", reference_accuracy, current_accuracy, t
        )

    def precision_drift(
        self,
        reference_precision: float,
        current_precision: float,
        threshold: float | None = None,
    ) -> DriftResult:
        """
        Detect drift in model precision.

        Parameters
        ----------
        reference_precision : float
            Baseline precision value in [0, 1].
        current_precision : float
            Current precision value in [0, 1].
        threshold : float or None, optional
            Minimum absolute change to flag drift. Falls back to
            ``self.threshold`` when ``None``.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            ``metric_name`` : str
                Always ``"Precision Drift"``.
            ``reference_value`` : float
                Baseline precision.
            ``current_value`` : float
                Current precision.
            ``precision_change`` : float
                Signed change (current − reference).
            ``threshold`` : float
                Threshold used.
            ``drift_detected`` : bool
                ``True`` when ``|precision_change| > threshold``.
            ``drift_severity`` : str
                ``"none"`` | ``"low"`` | ``"medium"`` | ``"high"`` | ``"critical"``.
        """
        t = threshold if threshold is not None else self.threshold
        self._validate_metric_value(reference_precision, "reference_precision")
        self._validate_metric_value(current_precision, "current_precision")
        return self._scalar_drift(
            "Precision Drift",
            "precision_change",
            reference_precision,
            current_precision,
            t,
        )

    def recall_drift(
        self,
        reference_recall: float,
        current_recall: float,
        threshold: float | None = None,
    ) -> DriftResult:
        """
        Detect drift in model recall.

        Parameters
        ----------
        reference_recall : float
            Baseline recall value in [0, 1].
        current_recall : float
            Current recall value in [0, 1].
        threshold : float or None, optional
            Minimum absolute change to flag drift. Falls back to
            ``self.threshold`` when ``None``.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            ``metric_name`` : str
                Always ``"Recall Drift"``.
            ``reference_value`` : float
                Baseline recall.
            ``current_value`` : float
                Current recall.
            ``recall_change`` : float
                Signed change (current − reference).
            ``threshold`` : float
                Threshold used.
            ``drift_detected`` : bool
                ``True`` when ``|recall_change| > threshold``.
            ``drift_severity`` : str
                ``"none"`` | ``"low"`` | ``"medium"`` | ``"high"`` | ``"critical"``.
        """
        t = threshold if threshold is not None else self.threshold
        self._validate_metric_value(reference_recall, "reference_recall")
        self._validate_metric_value(current_recall, "current_recall")
        return self._scalar_drift(
            "Recall Drift", "recall_change", reference_recall, current_recall, t
        )

    def f1_drift(
        self,
        reference_f1: float,
        current_f1: float,
        threshold: float | None = None,
    ) -> DriftResult:
        """
        Detect drift in model F1 score.

        Parameters
        ----------
        reference_f1 : float
            Baseline F1 score in [0, 1].
        current_f1 : float
            Current F1 score in [0, 1].
        threshold : float or None, optional
            Minimum absolute change to flag drift. Falls back to
            ``self.threshold`` when ``None``.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            ``metric_name`` : str
                Always ``"F1 Score Drift"``.
            ``reference_value`` : float
                Baseline F1 score.
            ``current_value`` : float
                Current F1 score.
            ``f1_change`` : float
                Signed change (current − reference).
            ``threshold`` : float
                Threshold used.
            ``drift_detected`` : bool
                ``True`` when ``|f1_change| > threshold``.
            ``drift_severity`` : str
                ``"none"`` | ``"low"`` | ``"medium"`` | ``"high"`` | ``"critical"``.
        """
        t = threshold if threshold is not None else self.threshold
        self._validate_metric_value(reference_f1, "reference_f1")
        self._validate_metric_value(current_f1, "current_f1")
        return self._scalar_drift(
            "F1 Score Drift", "f1_change", reference_f1, current_f1, t
        )

    def auc_drift(
        self,
        reference_auc: float,
        current_auc: float,
        threshold: float | None = None,
    ) -> DriftResult:
        """
        Detect drift in AUC-ROC score.

        Parameters
        ----------
        reference_auc : float
            Baseline AUC-ROC value in [0, 1].
        current_auc : float
            Current AUC-ROC value in [0, 1].
        threshold : float or None, optional
            Minimum absolute change to flag drift. Falls back to
            ``self.threshold`` when ``None``.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            ``metric_name`` : str
                Always ``"AUC Drift"``.
            ``reference_value`` : float
                Baseline AUC-ROC.
            ``current_value`` : float
                Current AUC-ROC.
            ``auc_change`` : float
                Signed change (current − reference).
            ``threshold`` : float
                Threshold used.
            ``drift_detected`` : bool
                ``True`` when ``|auc_change| > threshold``.
            ``drift_severity`` : str
                ``"none"`` | ``"low"`` | ``"medium"`` | ``"high"`` | ``"critical"``.
        """
        t = threshold if threshold is not None else self.threshold
        self._validate_metric_value(reference_auc, "reference_auc")
        self._validate_metric_value(current_auc, "current_auc")
        return self._scalar_drift(
            "AUC Drift", "auc_change", reference_auc, current_auc, t
        )

    def performance_degradation_score(
        self,
        reference_metrics: dict[str, float],
        current_metrics: dict[str, float],
        weights: dict[str, float] | None = None,
    ) -> DriftResult:
        """
        Weighted composite performance degradation score.

        Accumulates only negative metric changes (degradations). Improvements
        are treated as zero contribution. Optional per-metric weights allow
        prioritising critical metrics.

        Parameters
        ----------
        reference_metrics : dict[str, float]
            Mapping of metric name to baseline value.
        current_metrics : dict[str, float]
            Mapping of metric name to current value.
        weights : dict[str, float] or None, optional
            Per-metric weights. When ``None``, all metrics are equally weighted.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            ``metric_name`` : str
                Always ``"Performance Degradation Score"``.
            ``degradation_score`` : float
                Weighted degradation. < 0.02 low, 0.02–0.05 medium,
                0.05–0.10 high, > 0.10 critical.
            ``individual_degradations`` : dict[str, float]
                Per-metric degradation contributions.
            ``drift_detected`` : bool
                ``True`` when ``degradation_score >= 0.02``.
            ``drift_severity`` : str
                ``"low"`` | ``"medium"`` | ``"high"`` | ``"critical"``.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If either metrics dict is empty, they share no common keys, or the
            sum of weights is zero.
        """
        if not reference_metrics:
            raise ValueError("reference_metrics must not be empty.")
        if not current_metrics:
            raise ValueError("current_metrics must not be empty.")
        common_keys = set(reference_metrics) & set(current_metrics)
        if not common_keys:
            raise ValueError(
                "reference_metrics and current_metrics share no common keys."
            )
        effective_weights = (
            weights if weights is not None else {k: 1.0 for k in reference_metrics}
        )
        total_weight = sum(effective_weights.values())
        if total_weight == 0:
            raise ValueError("Sum of weights must not be zero.")
        norm_weights = {k: v / total_weight for k, v in effective_weights.items()}
        degradation_scores: dict[str, float] = {}
        total_degradation = 0.0
        for key in common_keys:
            change = (current_metrics[key] - reference_metrics[key]) / (
                reference_metrics[key] + self._EPSILON
            )
            degradation = -change if change < 0.0 else 0.0
            degradation_scores[key] = degradation
            total_degradation += degradation * norm_weights.get(key, 0.0)
        if total_degradation < 0.02:
            severity, drift_detected = "low", False
        elif total_degradation < 0.05:
            severity, drift_detected = "medium", True
        elif total_degradation < 0.10:
            severity, drift_detected = "high", True
        else:
            severity, drift_detected = "critical", True
        logger.debug(
            "Performance degradation score: %.4f (%s)", total_degradation, severity
        )
        return {
            "metric_name": "Performance Degradation Score",
            "degradation_score": float(total_degradation),
            "individual_degradations": degradation_scores,
            "drift_detected": drift_detected,
            "drift_severity": severity,
        }

    def metric_stability_check(
        self,
        metric_history: list[float],
        window_size: int = 5,
        threshold: float | None = None,
    ) -> DriftResult:
        """
        Temporal stability check via rolling coefficient of variation and trend.

        Analyses the most recent ``window_size`` values from a metric history to
        detect instability (high variance or monotonic trend).

        Parameters
        ----------
        metric_history : list[float]
            Ordered list of historical metric values (oldest first).
        window_size : int, optional
            Number of recent values to analyse. Must be >= 2. Default is ``5``.
        threshold : float or None, optional
            CV / trend instability threshold. Falls back to ``self.threshold``
            when ``None``.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            ``metric_name`` : str
                Always ``"Metric Stability"``.
            ``stable`` : bool
                ``True`` when both CV and trend are below ``threshold``.
            ``coefficient_of_variation`` : float
                CV of the recent window (std / mean).
            ``trend`` : float
                Linear slope fitted to the recent window.
            ``mean`` : float
                Mean of the recent window.
            ``std`` : float
                Std of the recent window.
            ``instability_severity`` : str
                ``"none"`` | ``"low"`` | ``"medium"`` | ``"high"`` | ``"critical"``.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ``metric_history`` is empty or ``window_size < 2``.
        """
        t = threshold if threshold is not None else self.threshold
        if not metric_history:
            raise ValueError("metric_history must not be empty.")
        if window_size < 2:
            raise ValueError(f"window_size must be >= 2, got {window_size}.")
        if len(metric_history) < window_size:
            logger.debug(
                "Insufficient data for stability check (%d < %d).",
                len(metric_history),
                window_size,
            )
            return {
                "metric_name": "Metric Stability",
                "stable": True,
                "coefficient_of_variation": 0.0,
                "trend": 0.0,
                "mean": float(np.mean(metric_history)),
                "std": float(np.std(metric_history)),
                "instability_severity": "none",
                "message": "Insufficient data for stability check.",
            }
        recent = metric_history[-window_size:]
        mean_val = float(np.mean(recent))
        std_val = float(np.std(recent))
        cv = std_val / (mean_val + self._EPSILON)
        trend = float(np.polyfit(np.arange(len(recent)), recent, 1)[0])
        stable = bool(cv < t and abs(trend) < t)
        if cv < 0.05:
            severity = "low"
        elif cv < 0.1:
            severity = "medium"
        elif cv < 0.2:
            severity = "high"
        else:
            severity = "critical"
        return {
            "metric_name": "Metric Stability",
            "stable": stable,
            "coefficient_of_variation": cv,
            "trend": trend,
            "mean": mean_val,
            "std": std_val,
            "instability_severity": severity if not stable else "none",
        }


####################################################################################################
FILE: src\dlh_ai\ml\drift\prediction_drift.py
####################################################################################################


"""
Prediction drift detection.

Detects shifts in prediction distributions, class imbalance changes, confidence
drift, error distribution changes, and systematic prediction bias.
"""

import logging
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import ClassVar, Optional

import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

from .statistical_tests import _validate_arrays

logger = logging.getLogger("dlh_ai")

DriftResult = dict[str, object]


@dataclass
class PredictionDrift:
    """
    Prediction drift detectors for ML model outputs.

    All detection logic lives inside this class. Instantiate once with a
    threshold and call detection methods directly on the instance.

    Parameters
    ----------
    threshold : float, optional
        Default significance level / minimum change used when no per-call
        value is supplied. Must be a positive finite number. Default is
        ``0.05``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``threshold`` is not a positive finite number.
    """

    _EPSILON: ClassVar[float] = 1e-10

    threshold: float = field(default=0.05)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not np.isfinite(self.threshold) or self.threshold <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"threshold must be a positive finite number, got {self.threshold}."
            )

    def prediction_distribution_shift(
        self,
        reference_predictions: np.ndarray,
        current_predictions: np.ndarray,
        threshold: float | None = None,
    ) -> DriftResult:
        """
        Detect prediction score distribution shift via KS test.

        Parameters
        ----------
        reference_predictions : np.ndarray
            Baseline 1-D prediction score array.
        current_predictions : np.ndarray
            Current 1-D prediction score array.
        threshold : float or None, optional
            p-value significance level. Falls back to ``self.threshold`` when
            ``None``.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            ``metric_name`` : str
                Always ``"Prediction Distribution Shift"``.
            ``ks_statistic`` : float
                KS test statistic.
            ``p_value`` : float
                KS test p-value.
            ``prediction_dist_shift`` : float
                Alias of ``ks_statistic``.
            ``mean_shift`` : float
                Absolute change in mean prediction score.
            ``std_shift`` : float
                Absolute change in std of prediction scores.
            ``reference_mean`` : float
                Mean of reference predictions.
            ``current_mean`` : float
                Mean of current predictions.
            ``reference_std`` : float
                Std of reference predictions.
            ``current_std`` : float
                Std of current predictions.
            ``threshold`` : float
                Significance level used.
            ``drift_detected`` : bool
                ``True`` when ``p_value < threshold``.
            ``drift_severity`` : str
                ``"none"`` | ``"low"`` | ``"medium"`` | ``"high"`` | ``"critical"``.
        """
        t = threshold if threshold is not None else self.threshold
        _validate_arrays(
            reference_predictions, current_predictions, "prediction_distribution_shift"
        )
        logger.debug("Checking prediction distribution shift.")
        statistic, p_value = stats.ks_2samp(reference_predictions, current_predictions)
        drift_detected = bool(p_value < t)
        ref_mean = float(np.mean(reference_predictions))
        curr_mean = float(np.mean(current_predictions))
        ref_std = float(np.std(reference_predictions))
        curr_std = float(np.std(current_predictions))
        if statistic < 0.1:
            severity = "low"
        elif statistic < 0.2:
            severity = "medium"
        elif statistic < 0.3:
            severity = "high"
        else:
            severity = "critical"
        return {
            "metric_name": "Prediction Distribution Shift",
            "ks_statistic": float(statistic),
            "p_value": float(p_value),
            "prediction_dist_shift": float(statistic),
            "mean_shift": abs(curr_mean - ref_mean),
            "std_shift": abs(curr_std - ref_std),
            "reference_mean": ref_mean,
            "current_mean": curr_mean,
            "reference_std": ref_std,
            "current_std": curr_std,
            "threshold": float(t),
            "drift_detected": drift_detected,
            "drift_severity": severity if drift_detected else "none",
        }

    def class_imbalance_change(
        self,
        reference_predictions: np.ndarray,
        current_predictions: np.ndarray,
        threshold: float | None = None,
        num_classes: Optional[int] = None,
    ) -> DriftResult:
        """
        Detect per-class proportion changes for classification models.

        Parameters
        ----------
        reference_predictions : np.ndarray
            Baseline 1-D integer class label array.
        current_predictions : np.ndarray
            Current 1-D integer class label array.
        threshold : float or None, optional
            Minimum proportion change to flag a class as drifted. Falls back to
            ``self.threshold`` when ``None``.
        num_classes : int or None, optional
            Number of classes. Inferred from the data when ``None``.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            ``metric_name`` : str
                Always ``"Class Imbalance Change"``.
            ``max_proportion_change`` : float
                Maximum absolute proportion change across all classes.
            ``mean_proportion_change`` : float
                Mean absolute proportion change.
            ``changed_classes`` : list[dict]
                Per-class details for classes whose proportion changed beyond
                ``threshold``.
            ``reference_proportions`` : list[float]
                Per-class proportions in the reference window.
            ``current_proportions`` : list[float]
                Per-class proportions in the current window.
            ``threshold`` : float
                Threshold used.
            ``drift_detected`` : bool
                ``True`` when ``max_proportion_change > threshold``.
            ``drift_severity`` : str
                ``"none"`` | ``"low"`` | ``"medium"`` | ``"high"`` | ``"critical"``.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ``num_classes < 1``.
        """
        t = threshold if threshold is not None else self.threshold
        _validate_arrays(
            reference_predictions, current_predictions, "class_imbalance_change"
        )
        if num_classes is None:
            num_classes = int(
                len(
                    np.unique(
                        np.concatenate([reference_predictions, current_predictions])
                    )
                )
            )
        elif num_classes < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"num_classes must be >= 1, got {num_classes}.")
        logger.debug("Checking class imbalance change over %d classes.", num_classes)
        ref_props = np.bincount(
            reference_predictions.astype(int), minlength=num_classes
        ) / len(reference_predictions)
        curr_props = np.bincount(
            current_predictions.astype(int), minlength=num_classes
        ) / len(current_predictions)
        prop_changes = np.abs(curr_props - ref_props)
        max_change = float(np.max(prop_changes))
        drift_detected = bool(max_change > t)
        changed_classes = [
            {
                "class": int(i),
                "reference_proportion": float(ref_props[i]),
                "current_proportion": float(curr_props[i]),
                "change": float(prop_changes[i]),
            }
            for i in range(num_classes)
            if prop_changes[i] > t
        ]
        if max_change < 0.05:
            severity = "low"
        elif max_change < 0.1:
            severity = "medium"
        elif max_change < 0.2:
            severity = "high"
        else:
            severity = "critical"
        return {
            "metric_name": "Class Imbalance Change",
            "max_proportion_change": max_change,
            "mean_proportion_change": float(np.mean(prop_changes)),
            "changed_classes": changed_classes,
            "reference_proportions": ref_props.tolist(),
            "current_proportions": curr_props.tolist(),
            "threshold": float(t),
            "drift_detected": drift_detected,
            "drift_severity": severity if drift_detected else "none",
        }

    def prediction_confidence_drift(
        self,
        reference_confidences: np.ndarray,
        current_confidences: np.ndarray,
        threshold: float | None = None,
    ) -> DriftResult:
        """
        Detect drift in prediction confidence / probability scores.

        Parameters
        ----------
        reference_confidences : np.ndarray
            Baseline 1-D confidence score array (values in [0, 1]).
        current_confidences : np.ndarray
            Current 1-D confidence score array (values in [0, 1]).
        threshold : float or None, optional
            Minimum mean confidence change to flag drift. Falls back to
            ``self.threshold`` when ``None``.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            ``metric_name`` : str
                Always ``"Prediction Confidence Drift"``.
            ``mean_confidence_change`` : float
                Absolute change in mean confidence.
            ``std_confidence_change`` : float
                Absolute change in confidence std.
            ``reference_mean_confidence`` : float
                Mean of reference confidence scores.
            ``current_mean_confidence`` : float
                Mean of current confidence scores.
            ``reference_std_confidence`` : float
                Std of reference confidence scores.
            ``current_std_confidence`` : float
                Std of current confidence scores.
            ``low_confidence_ref`` : float
                Fraction of reference predictions with confidence < 0.5.
            ``low_confidence_curr`` : float
                Fraction of current predictions with confidence < 0.5.
            ``high_confidence_ref`` : float
                Fraction of reference predictions with confidence > 0.9.
            ``high_confidence_curr`` : float
                Fraction of current predictions with confidence > 0.9.
            ``ks_statistic`` : float
                KS statistic between confidence distributions.
            ``p_value`` : float
                KS p-value.
            ``threshold`` : float
                Threshold used.
            ``drift_detected`` : bool
                ``True`` when ``mean_confidence_change > threshold`` or
                ``p_value < 0.05``.
            ``drift_severity`` : str
                ``"none"`` | ``"low"`` | ``"medium"`` | ``"high"`` | ``"critical"``.
        """
        t = threshold if threshold is not None else self.threshold
        _validate_arrays(
            reference_confidences, current_confidences, "prediction_confidence_drift"
        )
        logger.debug("Checking prediction confidence drift.")
        ref_mean = float(np.mean(reference_confidences))
        curr_mean = float(np.mean(current_confidences))
        ref_std = float(np.std(reference_confidences))
        curr_std = float(np.std(current_confidences))
        mean_change = abs(curr_mean - ref_mean)
        statistic, p_value = stats.ks_2samp(reference_confidences, current_confidences)
        drift_detected = bool(mean_change > t or p_value < 0.05)
        if mean_change < 0.02:
            severity = "low"
        elif mean_change < 0.05:
            severity = "medium"
        elif mean_change < 0.1:
            severity = "high"
        else:
            severity = "critical"
        return {
            "metric_name": "Prediction Confidence Drift",
            "mean_confidence_change": float(mean_change),
            "std_confidence_change": abs(curr_std - ref_std),
            "reference_mean_confidence": ref_mean,
            "current_mean_confidence": curr_mean,
            "reference_std_confidence": ref_std,
            "current_std_confidence": curr_std,
            "low_confidence_ref": float(
                np.sum(reference_confidences < 0.5) / len(reference_confidences)
            ),
            "low_confidence_curr": float(
                np.sum(current_confidences < 0.5) / len(current_confidences)
            ),
            "high_confidence_ref": float(
                np.sum(reference_confidences > 0.9) / len(reference_confidences)
            ),
            "high_confidence_curr": float(
                np.sum(current_confidences > 0.9) / len(current_confidences)
            ),
            "ks_statistic": float(statistic),
            "p_value": float(p_value),
            "threshold": float(t),
            "drift_detected": drift_detected,
            "drift_severity": severity if drift_detected else "none",
        }

    def prediction_error_drift(
        self,
        reference_errors: np.ndarray,
        current_errors: np.ndarray,
        threshold: float | None = None,
    ) -> DriftResult:
        """
        Detect drift in prediction error distribution (regression).

        Compares MAE and RMSE of residuals between the reference and current
        windows using both absolute and relative changes.

        Parameters
        ----------
        reference_errors : np.ndarray
            Baseline 1-D residual array (prediction − actual).
        current_errors : np.ndarray
            Current 1-D residual array.
        threshold : float or None, optional
            Minimum relative change (fraction) to flag drift. Falls back to
            ``self.threshold`` when ``None``.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            ``metric_name`` : str
                Always ``"Prediction Error Drift"``.
            ``mae_change`` : float
                Absolute change in MAE.
            ``rmse_change`` : float
                Absolute change in RMSE.
            ``mae_relative_change`` : float
                MAE change relative to reference MAE.
            ``rmse_relative_change`` : float
                RMSE change relative to reference RMSE.
            ``reference_mae`` / ``current_mae`` : float
                Reference and current MAE values.
            ``reference_rmse`` / ``current_rmse`` : float
                Reference and current RMSE values.
            ``ks_statistic`` : float
                KS statistic on absolute residuals.
            ``p_value`` : float
                KS p-value.
            ``threshold`` : float
                Threshold used.
            ``drift_detected`` : bool
                ``True`` when relative MAE or RMSE change exceeds ``threshold``.
            ``drift_severity`` : str
                ``"none"`` | ``"low"`` | ``"medium"`` | ``"high"`` | ``"critical"``.
        """
        t = threshold if threshold is not None else self.threshold
        _validate_arrays(reference_errors, current_errors, "prediction_error_drift")
        logger.debug("Checking prediction error drift.")
        ref_mae = float(np.mean(np.abs(reference_errors)))
        curr_mae = float(np.mean(np.abs(current_errors)))
        ref_rmse = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(reference_errors**2)))
        curr_rmse = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(current_errors**2)))
        mae_change = abs(curr_mae - ref_mae)
        rmse_change = abs(curr_rmse - ref_rmse)
        mae_rel = mae_change / (ref_mae + self._EPSILON)
        rmse_rel = rmse_change / (ref_rmse + self._EPSILON)
        statistic, p_value = stats.ks_2samp(
            np.abs(reference_errors), np.abs(current_errors)
        )
        drift_detected = bool(mae_rel > t or rmse_rel > t)
        max_rel = max(mae_rel, rmse_rel)
        if max_rel < 0.1:
            severity = "low"
        elif max_rel < 0.2:
            severity = "medium"
        elif max_rel < 0.5:
            severity = "high"
        else:
            severity = "critical"
        return {
            "metric_name": "Prediction Error Drift",
            "mae_change": float(mae_change),
            "rmse_change": float(rmse_change),
            "mae_relative_change": float(mae_rel),
            "rmse_relative_change": float(rmse_rel),
            "reference_mae": ref_mae,
            "current_mae": curr_mae,
            "reference_rmse": ref_rmse,
            "current_rmse": curr_rmse,
            "ks_statistic": float(statistic),
            "p_value": float(p_value),
            "threshold": float(t),
            "drift_detected": drift_detected,
            "drift_severity": severity if drift_detected else "none",
        }

    def prediction_bias_drift(
        self,
        reference_predictions: np.ndarray,
        reference_actuals: np.ndarray,
        current_predictions: np.ndarray,
        current_actuals: np.ndarray,
        threshold: float | None = None,
    ) -> DriftResult:
        """
        Detect change in systematic prediction bias (mean signed error).

        Bias is defined as the mean of (prediction − actual). A change in bias
        indicates that the model has become systematically over- or under-predicting.

        Parameters
        ----------
        reference_predictions : np.ndarray
            Baseline 1-D prediction array.
        reference_actuals : np.ndarray
            Baseline 1-D ground-truth array.
        current_predictions : np.ndarray
            Current 1-D prediction array.
        current_actuals : np.ndarray
            Current 1-D ground-truth array.
        threshold : float or None, optional
            Minimum absolute bias change to flag drift. Falls back to
            ``self.threshold`` when ``None``.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            ``metric_name`` : str
                Always ``"Prediction Bias Drift"``.
            ``bias_change`` : float
                Absolute change in bias (|current_bias − reference_bias|).
            ``reference_bias`` : float
                Mean signed error in the reference window.
            ``current_bias`` : float
                Mean signed error in the current window.
            ``reference_relative_bias`` : float
                Reference bias normalised by reference actual std.
            ``current_relative_bias`` : float
                Current bias normalised by current actual std.
            ``threshold`` : float
                Threshold used.
            ``drift_detected`` : bool
                ``True`` when ``bias_change > threshold``.
            ``drift_severity`` : str
                ``"none"`` | ``"low"`` | ``"medium"`` | ``"high"`` | ``"critical"``.
        """
        t = threshold if threshold is not None else self.threshold
        _validate_arrays(
            reference_predictions,
            reference_actuals,
            "reference (predictions vs actuals)",
        )
        _validate_arrays(
            current_predictions, current_actuals, "current (predictions vs actuals)"
        )
        logger.debug("Checking prediction bias drift.")
        ref_bias = float(np.mean(reference_predictions - reference_actuals))
        curr_bias = float(np.mean(current_predictions - current_actuals))
        bias_change = abs(curr_bias - ref_bias)
        drift_detected = bool(bias_change > t)
        if bias_change < 0.02:
            severity = "low"
        elif bias_change < 0.05:
            severity = "medium"
        elif bias_change < 0.1:
            severity = "high"
        else:
            severity = "critical"
        return {
            "metric_name": "Prediction Bias Drift",
            "bias_change": float(bias_change),
            "reference_bias": ref_bias,
            "current_bias": curr_bias,
            "reference_relative_bias": ref_bias
            / (float(np.std(reference_actuals)) + self._EPSILON),
            "current_relative_bias": curr_bias
            / (float(np.std(current_actuals)) + self._EPSILON),
            "threshold": float(t),
            "drift_detected": drift_detected,
            "drift_severity": severity if drift_detected else "none",
        }

"""
Stability metrics for drift detection: PSI, CSI, and DSI.

These metrics quantify the degree to which a feature's distribution has shifted
compared to a reference baseline, and are widely used in production ML monitoring.
"""

import logging
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import ClassVar

import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

from .statistical_tests import _validate_arrays

logger = logging.getLogger("dlh_ai")

DriftResult = dict[str, float | bool | str]


@dataclass
class StabilityMetrics:
    """
    Stability metrics (PSI, CSI, DSI) for distribution drift detection.

    Instantiate once with a default bin count and call metric methods
    directly on the instance.

    Parameters
    ----------
    bins : int, optional
        Default number of histogram bins used when no per-call value is
        supplied. Must be >= 2. Default is ``10``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``bins < 2``.
    """

    _EPSILON: ClassVar[float] = 1e-10

    bins: int = field(default=10)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.bins < 2:
            raise ValueError(f"bins must be >= 2, got {self.bins}.")

    @staticmethod
    def _psi_interpretation(psi: float) -> str:
        if psi < 0.1:
            return "No significant change detected."
        if psi < 0.2:
            return "Moderate change detected — investigate further."
        return "Significant change detected — consider model retraining."

    @staticmethod
    def _psi_severity(psi: float) -> tuple[str, bool]:
        if psi < 0.1:
            return "low", False
        if psi < 0.2:
            return "medium", True
        if psi < 0.3:
            return "high", True
        return "critical", True

    def population_stability_index(
        self,
        reference_data: np.ndarray,
        current_data: np.ndarray,
        bins: int | None = None,
        bin_edges: np.ndarray | None = None,
    ) -> DriftResult:
        """
        Population Stability Index (PSI).

        Industry-standard metric for measuring distribution shift. Widely used
        in credit risk modelling and financial services ML monitoring.

        Parameters
        ----------
        reference_data : np.ndarray
            Baseline 1-D sample array.
        current_data : np.ndarray
            Current 1-D sample array.
        bins : int or None, optional
            Number of histogram bins. Falls back to ``self.bins`` when ``None``.
        bin_edges : np.ndarray or None, optional
            Pre-computed bin edges. When provided, ``bins`` is ignored and
            these edges are used directly.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            ``metric_name`` : str
                Always ``"Population Stability Index"``.
            ``psi_score`` : float
                PSI value. < 0.1 no change, 0.1–0.2 moderate, > 0.2 significant.
            ``bins`` : int
                Number of bins used.
            ``drift_detected`` : bool
                ``True`` when ``psi_score >= 0.1``.
            ``drift_severity`` : str
                ``"low"`` | ``"medium"`` | ``"high"`` | ``"critical"``.
            ``interpretation`` : str
                Human-readable PSI interpretation string.
        """
        b = bins if bins is not None else self.bins
        _validate_arrays(reference_data, current_data, "population_stability_index")
        logger.debug("Computing PSI with %d bins.", b)
        edges = (
            bin_edges
            if bin_edges is not None
            else np.histogram_bin_edges(reference_data, bins=b)
        )
        actual_bins = len(edges) - 1
        ref_hist, _ = np.histogram(reference_data, bins=edges)
        curr_hist, _ = np.histogram(current_data, bins=edges)
        ref_pct = (ref_hist.astype(float) + self._EPSILON) / (
            ref_hist.sum() + actual_bins * self._EPSILON
        )
        curr_pct = (curr_hist.astype(float) + self._EPSILON) / (
            curr_hist.sum() + actual_bins * self._EPSILON
        )
        psi = float(np.sum((curr_pct - ref_pct) * np.log(curr_pct / ref_pct)))
        severity, drift_detected = self._psi_severity(psi)
        return {
            "metric_name": "Population Stability Index",
            "psi_score": psi,
            "bins": actual_bins,
            "drift_detected": drift_detected,
            "drift_severity": severity,
            "interpretation": self._psi_interpretation(psi),
        }

    def characteristic_stability_index(
        self,
        reference_data: np.ndarray,
        current_data: np.ndarray,
        bins: int | None = None,
    ) -> DriftResult:
        """
        Characteristic Stability Index (CSI).

        Measures the maximum relative bin deviation between distributions.
        More sensitive to tail shifts than PSI.

        Parameters
        ----------
        reference_data : np.ndarray
            Baseline 1-D sample array.
        current_data : np.ndarray
            Current 1-D sample array.
        bins : int or None, optional
            Number of histogram bins. Falls back to ``self.bins`` when ``None``.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            ``metric_name`` : str
                Always ``"Characteristic Stability Index"``.
            ``csi_score`` : float
                Maximum relative bin deviation. < 0.1 stable, 0.1–0.25 moderate,
                0.25–0.5 high, > 0.5 critical.
            ``bins`` : int
                Number of bins used.
            ``drift_detected`` : bool
                ``True`` when ``csi_score >= 0.1``.
            ``drift_severity`` : str
                ``"low"`` | ``"medium"`` | ``"high"`` | ``"critical"``.
        """
        b = bins if bins is not None else self.bins
        _validate_arrays(reference_data, current_data, "characteristic_stability_index")
        logger.debug("Computing CSI with %d bins.", b)
        edges = np.histogram_bin_edges(reference_data, bins=b)
        ref_hist, _ = np.histogram(reference_data, bins=edges)
        curr_hist, _ = np.histogram(current_data, bins=edges)
        ref_pct = (ref_hist.astype(float) + self._EPSILON) / (
            ref_hist.sum() + b * self._EPSILON
        )
        curr_pct = (curr_hist.astype(float) + self._EPSILON) / (
            curr_hist.sum() + b * self._EPSILON
        )
        csi = float(np.max(np.abs((curr_pct - ref_pct) / ref_pct)))
        if csi < 0.1:
            severity, drift_detected = "low", False
        elif csi < 0.25:
            severity, drift_detected = "medium", True
        elif csi < 0.5:
            severity, drift_detected = "high", True
        else:
            severity, drift_detected = "critical", True
        return {
            "metric_name": "Characteristic Stability Index",
            "csi_score": csi,
            "bins": b,
            "drift_detected": drift_detected,
            "drift_severity": severity,
        }

    def data_stability_index(
        self,
        reference_data: np.ndarray,
        current_data: np.ndarray,
    ) -> DriftResult:
        """
        Data Stability Index (DSI).

        Composite of normalised mean, variance, skewness and kurtosis shifts.
        Provides a single score summarising overall distributional change.

        Parameters
        ----------
        reference_data : np.ndarray
            Baseline 1-D sample array.
        current_data : np.ndarray
            Current 1-D sample array.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            ``metric_name`` : str
                Always ``"Data Stability Index"``.
            ``dsi_score`` : float
                Composite DSI. < 0.5 stable, 0.5–1.0 moderate, 1.0–2.0 high,
                > 2.0 critical.
            ``mean_shift`` : float
                Normalised mean shift (|Δμ| / σ_ref).
            ``variance_shift`` : float
                Normalised std shift (|Δσ| / σ_ref).
            ``skewness_shift`` : float
                Absolute change in skewness.
            ``kurtosis_shift`` : float
                Absolute change in excess kurtosis, scaled by 1/10.
            ``drift_detected`` : bool
                ``True`` when ``dsi_score >= 0.5``.
            ``drift_severity`` : str
                ``"low"`` | ``"medium"`` | ``"high"`` | ``"critical"``.
        """
        _validate_arrays(reference_data, current_data, "data_stability_index")
        logger.debug("Computing DSI.")
        ref_std = float(np.std(reference_data))
        mean_shift = abs(
            float(np.mean(current_data)) - float(np.mean(reference_data))
        ) / (ref_std + self._EPSILON)
        variance_shift = abs(float(np.std(current_data)) - ref_std) / (
            ref_std + self._EPSILON
        )
        skew_shift = abs(
            float(stats.skew(current_data)) - float(stats.skew(reference_data))
        )
        kurt_shift = (
            abs(
                float(stats.kurtosis(current_data))
                - float(stats.kurtosis(reference_data))
            )
            / 10.0
        )
        dsi = mean_shift + variance_shift + skew_shift + kurt_shift
        if dsi < 0.5:
            severity, drift_detected = "low", False
        elif dsi < 1.0:
            severity, drift_detected = "medium", True
        elif dsi < 2.0:
            severity, drift_detected = "high", True
        else:
            severity, drift_detected = "critical", True
        return {
            "metric_name": "Data Stability Index",
            "dsi_score": float(dsi),
            "mean_shift": float(mean_shift),
            "variance_shift": float(variance_shift),
            "skewness_shift": float(skew_shift),
            "kurtosis_shift": float(kurt_shift),
            "drift_detected": drift_detected,
            "drift_severity": severity,
        }

"""
Statistical hypothesis tests for drift detection.

Provides KS, Chi-Square, Anderson-Darling and Mann-Whitney U tests
to detect distributional shifts between reference and current datasets.
"""

import logging
import warnings
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

logger = logging.getLogger("dlh_ai")

DriftResult = dict[str, float | bool | str | None]


def _validate_arrays(
    reference: np.ndarray, current: np.ndarray, name: str = "data"
) -> None:
    """
    Validate that both arrays are non-empty 1-D numpy arrays.

    Shared validation helper imported by all drift detection modules.

    Parameters
    ----------
    reference : np.ndarray
        Baseline data array.
    current : np.ndarray
        Current data array.
    name : str, optional
        Label used in error messages to identify the calling context.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If either input is not a ``numpy.ndarray``.
    ValueError
        If either array is not 1-dimensional or is empty.
    """
    for label, arr in (("reference", reference), ("current", current)):
        if not isinstance(arr, np.ndarray):
            raise TypeError(
                f"{name} '{label}' must be a numpy.ndarray, got {type(arr).__name__}."
            )
        if arr.ndim != 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{name} '{label}' must be 1-dimensional, got shape {arr.shape}."
            )
        if arr.size == 0:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} '{label}' must not be empty.")


@dataclass
class StatisticalTests:
    """
    Statistical hypothesis tests for distribution drift detection.

    All test logic is implemented inside this class. Instantiate once with a
    significance threshold and call test methods directly on the instance.

    Parameters
    ----------
    threshold : float, optional
        Default p-value significance level used when no per-call threshold is
        supplied. Must satisfy ``0 < threshold < 1``. Default is ``0.05``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``threshold`` is not in the open interval (0, 1).
    """

    threshold: float = field(default=0.05)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not 0.0 < self.threshold < 1.0:
            raise ValueError(f"threshold must be in (0, 1), got {self.threshold}.")

    @staticmethod
    def _ks_severity(statistic: float) -> str:
        if statistic < 0.1:
            return "low"
        if statistic < 0.2:
            return "medium"
        if statistic < 0.3:
            return "high"
        return "critical"

    def kolmogorov_smirnov_test(
        self,
        reference_data: np.ndarray,
        current_data: np.ndarray,
        threshold: float | None = None,
    ) -> DriftResult:
        """
        Two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test for distribution drift.

        Parameters
        ----------
        reference_data : np.ndarray
            Baseline 1-D sample array.
        current_data : np.ndarray
            Current 1-D sample array.
        threshold : float or None, optional
            p-value significance level. Falls back to ``self.threshold`` when
            ``None``.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            ``test_name`` : str
                Always ``"Kolmogorov-Smirnov"``.
            ``statistic`` : float
                KS test statistic D (maximum absolute CDF difference).
            ``p_value`` : float
                Two-sided p-value.
            ``threshold`` : float
                Significance level used.
            ``drift_detected`` : bool
                ``True`` when ``p_value < threshold``.
            ``drift_severity`` : str
                ``"none"`` | ``"low"`` | ``"medium"`` | ``"high"`` | ``"critical"``.
        """
        t = threshold if threshold is not None else self.threshold
        _validate_arrays(reference_data, current_data, "kolmogorov_smirnov_test")
        logger.debug(
            "Running KS test on %d vs %d samples.",
            len(reference_data),
            len(current_data),
        )
        statistic, p_value = stats.ks_2samp(reference_data, current_data)
        drift_detected = bool(p_value < t)
        return {
            "test_name": "Kolmogorov-Smirnov",
            "statistic": float(statistic),
            "p_value": float(p_value),
            "threshold": float(t),
            "drift_detected": drift_detected,
            "drift_severity": self._ks_severity(float(statistic))
            if drift_detected
            else "none",
        }

    def chi_square_test(
        self,
        reference_data: np.ndarray,
        current_data: np.ndarray,
        bins: int = 10,
        threshold: float | None = None,
    ) -> DriftResult:
        """
        Chi-Square goodness-of-fit test on binned data.

        Parameters
        ----------
        reference_data : np.ndarray
            Baseline 1-D sample array.
        current_data : np.ndarray
            Current 1-D sample array.
        bins : int, optional
            Number of histogram bins. Must be >= 2. Default is ``10``.
        threshold : float or None, optional
            p-value significance level. Falls back to ``self.threshold`` when
            ``None``.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            ``test_name`` : str
                Always ``"Chi-Square"``.
            ``statistic`` : float
                Chi-Square test statistic.
            ``p_value`` : float
                p-value of the test.
            ``threshold`` : float
                Significance level used.
            ``bins`` : int
                Number of bins used.
            ``drift_detected`` : bool
                ``True`` when ``p_value < threshold``.
            ``drift_severity`` : str
                ``"none"`` | ``"low"`` | ``"medium"`` | ``"high"`` | ``"critical"``.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ``bins < 2``.
        """
        t = threshold if threshold is not None else self.threshold
        _validate_arrays(reference_data, current_data, "chi_square_test")
        if bins < 2:
            raise ValueError(f"bins must be >= 2, got {bins}.")
        logger.debug("Running Chi-Square test with %d bins.", bins)
        combined = np.concatenate([reference_data, current_data])
        bin_edges = np.histogram_bin_edges(combined, bins=bins)
        ref_freq, _ = np.histogram(reference_data, bins=bin_edges)
        curr_freq, _ = np.histogram(current_data, bins=bin_edges)
        ref_freq = ref_freq.astype(float) + 1e-10
        curr_freq = curr_freq.astype(float) + 1e-10
        ref_freq = ref_freq / ref_freq.sum() * curr_freq.sum()
        statistic, p_value = stats.chisquare(curr_freq, ref_freq)
        drift_detected = bool(p_value < t)
        if statistic < bins:
            severity = "low"
        elif statistic < bins * 2:
            severity = "medium"
        elif statistic < bins * 3:
            severity = "high"
        else:
            severity = "critical"
        return {
            "test_name": "Chi-Square",
            "statistic": float(statistic),
            "p_value": float(p_value),
            "threshold": float(t),
            "bins": int(bins),
            "drift_detected": drift_detected,
            "drift_severity": severity if drift_detected else "none",
        }

    def anderson_darling_test(
        self,
        reference_data: np.ndarray,
        current_data: np.ndarray,
        threshold: float | None = None,
    ) -> DriftResult:
        """
        Anderson-Darling two-sample test via ``scipy.stats.anderson_ksamp``.

        More sensitive to distribution tails than the KS test.

        Parameters
        ----------
        reference_data : np.ndarray
            Baseline 1-D sample array.
        current_data : np.ndarray
            Current 1-D sample array.
        threshold : float or None, optional
            p-value significance level. Falls back to ``self.threshold`` when
            ``None``.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            ``test_name`` : str
                Always ``"Anderson-Darling"``.
            ``statistic`` : float
                Anderson-Darling test statistic.
            ``critical_value`` : float
                Critical value at the chosen significance level.
            ``threshold`` : float
                Significance level used.
            ``drift_detected`` : bool
                ``True`` when ``p_value < threshold``.
            ``drift_severity`` : str
                ``"none"`` | ``"low"`` | ``"medium"`` | ``"high"`` | ``"critical"``.
        """
        t = threshold if threshold is not None else self.threshold
        _validate_arrays(reference_data, current_data, "anderson_darling_test")
        logger.debug("Running Anderson-Darling test.")
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
            result = stats.anderson_ksamp([reference_data, current_data])
        statistic = float(result.statistic)
        p_value = float(result.pvalue)
        _std_levels = np.array([0.25, 0.10, 0.05, 0.025, 0.01, 0.005, 0.001])
        if hasattr(result, "critical_values"):
            _cv_array = np.asarray(result.critical_values)
        else:
            _cv_array = np.array([0.325, 1.226, 1.961, 2.718, 3.752, 4.592, 6.546])
        closest_idx = int(np.argmin(np.abs(_std_levels - t)))
        critical_value = float(_cv_array[closest_idx])
        drift_detected = bool(p_value < t)
        if statistic < 0.5:
            severity = "low"
        elif statistic < 1.0:
            severity = "medium"
        elif statistic < 2.0:
            severity = "high"
        else:
            severity = "critical"
        return {
            "test_name": "Anderson-Darling",
            "statistic": statistic,
            "critical_value": critical_value,
            "threshold": float(t),
            "drift_detected": drift_detected,
            "drift_severity": severity if drift_detected else "none",
        }

    def mann_whitney_test(
        self,
        reference_data: np.ndarray,
        current_data: np.ndarray,
        threshold: float | None = None,
    ) -> DriftResult:
        """
        Mann-Whitney U non-parametric two-sample test.

        Suitable for non-normal distributions and ordinal data.

        Parameters
        ----------
        reference_data : np.ndarray
            Baseline 1-D sample array.
        current_data : np.ndarray
            Current 1-D sample array.
        threshold : float or None, optional
            p-value significance level. Falls back to ``self.threshold`` when
            ``None``.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            ``test_name`` : str
                Always ``"Mann-Whitney U"``.
            ``statistic`` : float
                Mann-Whitney U statistic.
            ``p_value`` : float
                Two-sided p-value.
            ``effect_size`` : float
                Common language effect size in [-1, 1].
            ``threshold`` : float
                Significance level used.
            ``drift_detected`` : bool
                ``True`` when ``p_value < threshold``.
            ``drift_severity`` : str
                ``"none"`` | ``"low"`` | ``"medium"`` | ``"high"`` | ``"critical"``.
        """
        t = threshold if threshold is not None else self.threshold
        _validate_arrays(reference_data, current_data, "mann_whitney_test")
        logger.debug("Running Mann-Whitney U test.")
        statistic, p_value = stats.mannwhitneyu(
            reference_data, current_data, alternative="two-sided"
        )
        drift_detected = bool(p_value < t)
        n1, n2 = len(reference_data), len(current_data)
        effect_size = float(1.0 - (2.0 * statistic) / (n1 * n2))
        abs_effect = abs(effect_size)
        if abs_effect < 0.1:
            severity = "low"
        elif abs_effect < 0.3:
            severity = "medium"
        elif abs_effect < 0.5:
            severity = "high"
        else:
            severity = "critical"
        return {
            "test_name": "Mann-Whitney U",
            "statistic": float(statistic),
            "p_value": float(p_value),
            "effect_size": effect_size,
            "threshold": float(t),
            "drift_detected": drift_detected,
            "drift_severity": severity if drift_detected else "none",
        }

class CAIClient:
    """Client for interacting with Cloudera AI (CAI) API.

    Parameters
    ----------
    project_id : str
        The CML project identifier.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> client = CAIClient(project_id="my-project-123")

    >>> job_config = client.job_config_template(
    ...     job_prefix_name="data-processing",
    ...     batch_no=1,
    ...     job_script="src/jobs/process_data.py"
    ... )
    >>> job = client.create_job(job_config)
    >>> job_run = client.create_job_run(job.id)
    """

    project_id: str

    @property
    def client(self) -> CMLServiceApi:
        """Get the CML service API client.

        Returns
        -------
        CMLServiceApi
            The default CML API client instance.

        Examples
        --------
        >>> cai = CAIClient()
        >>> api_client = cai.client
        """
        _ = cmlapi.default_client()
        return _

    def job_config_template(
        self,
        job_prefix_name: str,
        batch_no: int | None,
        job_script: str,
        cpu: int = 2,
        memory: int = 8,
        env: dict | None = None,
        runtime_identifier: str = "nexus.dlhdevuat.sbi.bank.in:9443/clouderadataservices/cloudera/cdsw/ml-runtime-jupyterlab-python3.11-ml:2026.03.03.v1",
    ) -> CreateJobRequest:
        """Create a CML job configuration template.

        Generates a job configuration with specified resources and runtime settings.
        If batch_no is provided, it will be included in the job name along with
        the current timestamp.

        Parameters
        ----------
        job_prefix_name : str
            Prefix for the job name.
        batch_no : int or None
            Batch number to include in job name. If None, only prefix is used.
        job_script : str
            Path to the script file to execute (e.g., "src/jobs/process_data.py").
        cpu : int, optional
            Number of CPU cores to allocate, by default 2.
        memory : int, optional
            Memory in GB to allocate, by default 8.
        env : dict or None, optional
            Environment variables as key-value pairs, by default None.
        runtime_identifier : str, optional
            Docker image identifier for the runtime environment.

        Returns
        -------
        CreateJobRequest
            Configured job request object ready for submission.

        Examples
        --------
        >>> client = CAIClient(project_id="proj-123")
        >>> # Create job config without batch number
        >>> config = client.job_config_template(
        ...     job_prefix_name="etl-pipeline",
        ...     batch_no=None,
        ...     job_script="src/jobs/etl.py",
        ...     cpu=4,
        ...     memory=16
        ... )
        >>>
        >>> # Create job config with batch number
        >>> config = client.job_config_template(
        ...     job_prefix_name="data-processing",
        ...     batch_no=5,
        ...     job_script="src/jobs/process.py",
        ...     env={"ENV": "production", "LOG_LEVEL": "INFO"}
        ... )

        Notes
        -----
        - The job timeout is set to 10 minutes (600 seconds).
        - Jobs are configured to be killed on timeout.
        - Spark runtime addons are automatically included for Spark 3.5.1.
        """
        # If there are batches then only we'll have batch name in job name
        name = (
            f"{job_prefix_name}-batch-{batch_no}-{str(datetime.now(tz=ZoneInfo('Asia/Kolkata')))}"
            if batch_no
            else job_prefix_name
        )

        return cmlapi.CreateJobRequest(
            name=name,
            project_id=self.project_id,
            script=job_script,
            cpu=cpu,
            memory=memory,
            environment=env,
            # NOTE - runtime should match with intended runtime docker image
            runtime_identifier=runtime_identifier,
            runtime_addon_identifiers=RUNTIME_IDENTIFIER,
            timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
            kill_on_timeout=True,
        )

    def create_job(self, job_config: CreateJobRequest) -> models.job.Job:
        """Create a new CML job.

        Submits a job configuration to CML and creates the job in the project.

        Parameters
        ----------
        job_config : CreateJobRequest
            Job configuration object created by job_config_template().

        Returns
        -------
        models.job.Job
            The created job object with job ID and metadata.

        Examples
        --------
        >>> client = CAIClient(project_id="proj-123")

        >>> config = client.job_config_template(
        ...     job_prefix_name="ml-training",
        ...     batch_no=1,
        ...     job_script="src/jobs/train_model.py"
        ... )
        >>> job = client.create_job(config)
        >>> print(f"Job created with ID: {job.id}")
        Job created with ID: job-abc-123

        See Also
        --------
        job_config_template : Create job configuration
        create_job_run : Execute a created job
        """
        job = self.client.create_job(job_config, project_id=self.project_id)
        logger.info(f"successfully created job with {job.id}")
        return job

    def create_job_run(self, job_id: str) -> models.job_run.JobRun:
        """Execute a CML job by creating a job run.

        Creates and starts a new run for an existing job.

        Parameters
        ----------
        job_id : str
            The unique identifier of the job to run.

        Returns
        -------
        models.job_run.JobRun
            The created job run object with run ID and status.

        Examples
        --------
        >>> client = CAIClient(project_id="proj-123")
        >>> # First create a job
        >>> config = client.job_config_template(
        ...     job_prefix_name="data-pipeline",
        ...     batch_no=None,
        ...     job_script="src/jobs/pipeline.py"
        ... )
        >>> job = client.create_job(config)
        >>>
        >>> # Then execute the job
        >>> job_run = client.create_job_run(job.id)
        >>> print(f"Job run started with ID: {job_run.id}")
        Job run started with ID: run-xyz-456

        See Also
        --------
        create_job : Create a new job
        _job_run_template : Generate job run configuration
        """
        job_run_config = self._job_run_template(job_id=job_id)
        run = self.client.create_job_run(
            job_run_config, job_id=job_id, project_id=setting.common.project_id
        )
        logger.info(f"successfully created job run {run.id}")
        return run

    def _job_run_template(self, job_id: str):
        """Create a job run configuration template.

        Internal method to generate the configuration for executing a job.

        Parameters
        ----------
        job_id : str
            The unique identifier of the job to run.

        Returns
        -------
        cmlapi.CreateJobRunRequest
            Job run request configuration object.

        Examples
        --------
        >>> client = CAIClient(project_id="proj-123")
        >>> run_config = client._job_run_template(job_id="job-abc-123")
        """
        return cmlapi.CreateJobRunRequest(project_id=self.project_id, job_id=job_id)
